cases.sentence: Не в радость обратятся тебе эти тринадцать ___.
options: глоток
глотка
глотки
глотков
cases.translation: These thirteen swallows will bring you no joy.
cases.explain: Numerals from five upwards (here тринадцать) take the genitive plural of the counted noun: тринадцать глотков.

cases.sentence: Не в радость обратятся ___ эти тринадцать глотков.
options: ты
тебя
тебе
тобой
cases.translation: These thirteen swallows will bring you no joy.
cases.explain: The person to whom something turns out well or badly is the indirect object, and indirect objects stand in the dative: обратятся тебе.

options: день
дня
дню
днём
cases.translation: May your day today be bright.
cases.explain: День is the subject of the clause (the thing said to be светел), and subjects stand in the nominative.

options: девочка
девочки
девочку
девочкой
cases.translation: Or will they knife me like a little girl?
cases.explain: The comparison «как…» copies the role of the direct object of зарежут, so девочка goes into the accusative; feminine nouns in -а take -у in the accusative: девочку.

cases.sentence: Я услышал сразу два полярных упрека: и в скучности, и в ___.
options: легкомыслие
легкомыслия
легкомыслию
легкомыслии
cases.translation: I heard two opposite reproaches at once: of being boring and of being frivolous.
cases.explain: «В» after a word like упрёк names the sphere of the accusation and requires the prepositional: упрёк в легкомыслии.

cases.sentence: Потому что я болен ___, но не подаю и вида.
options: душа
души
душу
душой
cases.translation: Because I am sick in my soul, but I never let it show.
cases.explain: With болен the part of you that is affected goes into the instrumental (болен душой, болен ногами), naming the respect in which one is ill.

cases.sentence: Смирись, Веничка, хотя бы на том, что твоя душа вместительнее ___ твоего.
options: ум
ума
уму
умом
cases.translation: Be content, Venichka, at least with the fact that your soul is more capacious than your mind.
cases.explain: A simple comparative like вместительнее is followed by the genitive of what is being compared: вместительнее ума.

cases.sentence: Выпьем за ___ – весь этот остаток кубанской.
options: понимание
понимания
пониманию
пониманием
cases.translation: Let's drink to understanding — all this last of the kubanskaya.
cases.explain: In a toast «выпить за…» the preposition за governs the accusative; понимание is inanimate and neuter, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

reading.ru: «Не в радость обратятся тебе эти тринадцать глотков», – подумал я, делая тринадцатый глоток.
reading.question: What does Venichka think to himself as he takes his thirteenth swallow?
options: That these thirteen swallows will bring him no joy
That he will stop drinking after this one
That the bottle is already empty
That the thirteenth swallow is the sweetest
reading.correct: That these thirteen swallows will bring him no joy
reading.explain: The chapter opens with him swallowing and simultaneously warning himself that the swallows will bring no joy.

reading.question: What does the inner voice say the second morning dose does if it is drunk straight from the bottle?
options: It clouds the soul, at least until the third dose
It cures the hangover completely
It has no effect whatsoever
It makes the angels sing
reading.correct: It clouds the soul, at least until the third dose
reading.explain: The voice insists that the second dose from the bottle darkens the soul until the third one is drunk from a glass — and that Venichka knows this perfectly well.

reading.question: What does Venichka assert about his own tomorrow?
options: That it is bright
That it is hopeless
That it will never come
That it belongs to the angels
reading.explain: He declares his tomorrow bright, and adds that our tomorrow is brighter than our yesterday and our today.

reading.ru: Но кто поручится, что наше послезавтра не будет хуже нашего позавчера?
reading.question: What doubt does Venichka raise straight after saying that tomorrow is brighter than yesterday?
options: Who can guarantee that the day after tomorrow will not be worse than the day before yesterday
Who will pay for the next bottle
Who will meet him on the platform
Who told the angels to keep quiet
reading.correct: Who can guarantee that the day after tomorrow will not be worse than the day before yesterday
reading.explain: The bright-tomorrow formula is immediately undercut by this question about the day after tomorrow.

reading.ru: Что меня там никто не встретит?
reading.question: Which of these is one of the misfortunes Venichka imagines the angels are silently fearing for him?
options: That nobody will meet him at Petushki
That he will lose his ticket
That the shops will not open
That he will forget the way to the Kremlin
reading.correct: That nobody will meet him at Petushki
reading.explain: He lists the possible disasters — nobody meeting him, the train going off the embankment, inspectors, being strangled asleep — and asks why the angels say nothing.

reading.ru: Почему же ангелы смущаются и молчат?
reading.question: How do the angels behave when Venichka starts talking about the joys awaiting him in Petushki?
options: They become embarrassed and fall silent
They laugh loudly at him
They congratulate him warmly
They tell him plainly what will happen
reading.correct: They become embarrassed and fall silent
reading.explain: Their embarrassed silence is exactly what puzzles and worries him.

reading.ru: И вообще, мозгов в тебе не очень много.
reading.question: What does the voice tell Venichka about his brains?
options: That he does not have very many of them
That they are sharper than anyone's
That drink has ruined them
That they are his only asset
reading.correct: That he does not have very many of them
reading.explain: The voice bluntly informs him that there are not very many brains in him — and asks whether he really did not know that.

reading.ru: Смирись, Веничка, хотя бы на том, что твоя душа вместительнее ума твоего.
reading.question: What consolation is Venichka told to settle for?
options: That his soul is more capacious than his mind
That his mind is quicker than other people's
That his memory is excellent
That his journey will be short
reading.correct: That his soul is more capacious than his mind
reading.explain: He is told to be content at least with the fact that his soul holds more than his mind does.

reading.ru: Совесть и вкус – это уже так много, что мозги делаются прямо излишними.
reading.question: Why, according to the voice, does Venichka have no need of a mind?
options: Because conscience and taste are already so much that brains become superfluous
Because a mind only leads to more drinking
Because the angels think for him
Because nobody around him uses one either
reading.correct: Because conscience and taste are already so much that brains become superfluous
reading.explain: Having conscience and taste on top of it is presented as making brains outright unnecessary.

reading.ru: Когда я услышал одновременно сразу два полярных упрека: и в скучности, и в легкомыслии.
reading.question: When does Venichka say he first realised he was a fool?
options: When he heard two opposite reproaches at once — of being boring and of being frivolous
When he first drank kubanskaya from the bottle
When the angels refused to answer him
When he saw Kramskoy's painting for the first time
reading.correct: When he heard two opposite reproaches at once — of being boring and of being frivolous
reading.explain: A clever man would not sink to frivolity and a frivolous one would not allow himself to be dull, yet he somehow managed to combine both.

reading.ru: Потому что я болен душой, но не подаю и вида.
reading.question: How does Venichka explain why he comes across as boring?
options: He is sick in his soul and spends all his strength simulating good health
He deliberately hides how clever he is
He has nothing at all on his mind
He is always too drunk to speak
reading.correct: He is sick in his soul and spends all his strength simulating good health
reading.explain: All his mental and physical strength goes into pretending to be spiritually healthy, which is why he is dull company.

reading.question: What does Venichka claim about his relationship to the truth?
options: Not that he knows it, only that he has come close enough to see it best
That he has known it since childhood
That there is no truth at all
That only the angels can reach it
reading.correct: Not that he knows it, only that he has come close enough to see it best
reading.explain: He denies knowing the truth or even standing right next to it, but says he is at the distance from which it is most convenient to look at it.

reading.ru: Как же не быть мне скушным и как же не пить кубанскую?
reading.question: What does Venichka say about his right to be boring and to drink kubanskaya?
options: That he has earned that right
That he is ashamed of it
That a doctor prescribed it
That he will give it up in Petushki
reading.correct: That he has earned that right
reading.explain: Carrying the world's sorrow inside him, he says, is what has earned him the right.

reading.ru: К примеру: вы видели „Неутешное горе“ Крамского?
reading.question: Which painting does Venichka use as his example?
options: Kramskoy's 'Inconsolable Grief'
Repin's 'Barge Haulers on the Volga'
Vasnetsov's 'Three Bogatyrs'
Bryullov's 'The Last Day of Pompeii'
reading.explain: He asks whether the reader has seen Kramskoy's picture and then imagines the frozen woman in it ignoring a cat smashing porcelain.

reading.ru: Она невозможно скушна и еще бы не была скушна!
reading.question: How does Venichka answer his own question about the grieving noblewoman in the painting?
options: That she is impossibly boring and frivolous in the highest degree at the same time
That she is neither boring nor frivolous
That she is simply tired after a long day
That she would rush about wringing her hands
reading.correct: That she is impossibly boring and frivolous in the highest degree at the same time
reading.explain: She is both, which is the point: he says the same combination applies to himself.

reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: With Venichka inviting everyone to watch how it is done
With Venichka falling asleep
With the train arriving at Petushki
With the angels finally answering him
reading.correct: With Venichka inviting everyone to watch how it is done
reading.explain: After proposing a toast to understanding he tells the reader to watch how the rest of the kubanskaya is drunk.

highlight.question: Which sentence asks why the angels grow embarrassed as soon as Venichka mentions the joys waiting for him in Petushki?
sentences: Ну пусть.
Пусть светел твой сегодняшний день.
Пусть твое завтра будет еще светлее.
Но почему же смущаются ангелы, чуть только ты заговоришь о радостях на петушинском перроне и после?
highlight.explain: The last sentence turns the bright wishes into a question about the angels' embarrassment.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka only rarely speaks as neatly and cleverly as he just did?
sentences: «Вот-вот!
Ты хорошо это, Веничка, сказал.
Наше завтра и так далее.
Очень складно и умно ты это сказал, ты редко говоришь так складно и умно.
highlight.explain: The praise in the fourth sentence carries the sting that such neat, clever speech is rare for him.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells Venichka to be content that his soul holds more than his mind does?
sentences: И вообще, мозгов в тебе не очень много.
Тебе ли, опять же, этого не знать?
Смирись, Веничка, хотя бы на том, что твоя душа вместительнее ума твоего.
Да и зачем тебе ум, коли у тебя есть совесть и сверх того еще вкус?
Совесть и вкус – это уже так много, что мозги делаются прямо излишними.
highlight.explain: Only the third sentence contains the instruction to resign himself to his soul being more capacious than his mind.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the two opposite reproaches that Venichka heard about himself at the same time?
sentences: «А вот когда.
Когда я услышал одновременно сразу два полярных упрека: и в скучности, и в легкомыслии.
Потому что если человек умен и скучен, он не опустится до легкомыслия.
А если он легкомыслен да умен – он скучным быть себе не позволит.
А вот я, рохля, как-то сумел сочетать.
highlight.explain: The second sentence names both reproaches — dullness and frivolity — while the rest only comment on them.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka has come near enough to the truth to view it most conveniently?
sentences: Я не утверждаю, что мне – теперь – истина уже известна или что я вплотную к ней подошел.
Вовсе нет.
Но я уже на такое расстояние к ней подошел, с которого ее удобнее всего рассмотреть.
highlight.explain: The first two sentences deny knowing the truth; the third states the distance from which it is best seen.

highlight.question: Which sentence asks why Venichka is a fool, a demon and an idle babbler all at once?
sentences: Вот так и я.
Теперь вы поняли, отчего я грустнее всех забулдыг?
Отчего я легковеснее всех идиотов, но и мрачнее всякого дерьма?
Отчего я и дурак, и демон, и пустомеля разом?
highlight.explain: The final question is the one that lists fool, demon and babbler together.
